rules.rule: Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §4 Database and migrations. Check: migrations are reversible or have an explicit `up`/`down`; indexes are added for new foreign keys and for columns that will be queried; column types and nullability match how the app actually uses the data; no data backfill inside a schema migration that would lock a large table; naming follows Rails conventions and existing WCA table vocabulary (§2.3). Cite the section, e.g. 'Style guide §4'. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs, architecture opinions, or anything RuboCop already enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §9 Tests. Check: the test asserts on behaviour rather than restating the implementation; factories are used over hand-built fixtures and only the traits the test needs are requested; no over-mocking of the object under test; descriptions say what is expected, not 'works correctly'; shared setup is not duplicated across examples. Also apply §1.2 (extract on the second occurrence) and §2 Naming. Cite the section, e.g. 'Style guide §9'. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report missing test coverage, bugs, or anything RuboCop enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §5 API design and §3.8 Controllers. Check: response shape is stable and serializer-driven rather than ad-hoc hashes; status codes are correct; new or changed endpoints keep the OpenAPI spec in step; params are permitted explicitly; controllers stay thin and push logic into models or service objects; no N+1 queries in the response path (§3.2 — watch for `includes` defeated by a later `to_a`, and for `count` where `size` is correct). Cite the section, e.g. 'Style guide §5'. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs, architecture opinions, or anything RuboCop enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §3.8 Controllers, plus §3.2 query performance. Check: controllers stay thin, logic belongs in models; strong params are explicit; authorization uses the existing `can_*?` helpers on User rather than hand-rolled role checks; no N+1 queries; failed writes are checked (§3.4 — a bare `update` or `save` whose return value is ignored is a defect, use the bang form or handle the false). Cite the section. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs, architecture opinions, or anything RuboCop enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §3.9 Jobs and rake tasks, plus §3.2 and §3.4. Check: any new cronjob is registered in `JobUtils::WCA_CRONJOBS`; the job is idempotent and safe to retry; work is batched rather than looping one record at a time; no N+1 queries inside the loop (hoist lookups out, or preload with `includes`); `update`/`save` return values are not silently discarded (§3.4); predicate helpers end in `?` and non-predicates do not use a `should_` prefix (§2.5); prefer non-mutating enumerable methods over in-place bang variants on local collections (§1.3). Cite the section, e.g. 'Style guide §3.2'. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs or anything RuboCop enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §3.9 Jobs and rake tasks. Check: the task is idempotent; it batches its work rather than loading everything into memory; it reports progress and failures rather than swallowing them (§1.6); no N+1 queries (§3.2); magic values are named constants (§1.4). Cite the section. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs or anything RuboCop enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §3 Ruby and Rails. Emphasise §3.1 reach for the Rails idiom; §3.2 query performance (use `size` on associations rather than `count`, never defeat `includes` with an intermediate `to_a`, avoid queries inside loops); §3.3 prefer declared associations and scopes over hand-rolled `where` chains; §3.4 do not ignore the return value of `update`/`save`; §3.5 `delete_all` skips callbacks — use `destroy_all` when callbacks matter; §3.6 polymorphism over `is_a?` type checks; §3.7 wrap multi-record writes in a transaction. Also §2 Naming and §1.4 no magic values. Cite the section, e.g. 'Style guide §3.3'. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs or anything RuboCop enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

This is the LEGACY frontend. Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §8 Legacy React (Webpacker / Semantic UI). CRITICAL: React Compiler is NOT enabled here, so manual `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`React.memo` are REQUIRED for referentially unstable values and must not be flagged as redundant — that rule applies only to next-frontend/. Check: Semantic UI components are used rather than bespoke markup; API calls go through `fetchWithAuthenticityToken`/`fetchJsonOrError`; i18n strings come from `i18n-js` rather than being hardcoded (§10); state lives in the existing contexts rather than new ad-hoc globals. Cite the section, e.g. 'Style guide §8'. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs or anything ESLint/Prettier enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

This is the NEXT.JS frontend. Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §6 and §7. CRITICAL: React Compiler IS enabled here, so manual `useMemo`, `useCallback` and `React.memo` are redundant and should be flagged for removal (§6.3) — the opposite rule applies in app/webpacker/. Check §6.1 server components by default, add `'use client'` only when the component genuinely needs interactivity or browser APIs; §6.2 types come from the generated schema in src/types/openapi.ts, never hand-written duplicates of API shapes; §6.4 data fetching goes through `useAPI()` / Tanstack Query with correct query keys, not bare fetch in an effect; §6.5 component structure and file placement. For styling, §7.1 use Chakra style props and theme tokens rather than raw CSS or hardcoded hex colours and pixel values, and §7.2 use the Chakra component that already exists rather than rebuilding it. Cite the section, e.g. 'Style guide §6.3'. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs or anything ESLint/Prettier enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §3 Ruby and Rails, §2 Naming and §1 Universal principles. Check §3.1 Rails idiom; §3.2 query performance including N+1s, `size` vs `count`, and `to_a` defeating `includes`; §3.4 unchecked `update`/`save` return values; §3.6 polymorphism over `is_a?`; §1.3 prefer immutable operations over in-place mutation; §1.4 no magic values; §1.5 comments explain why, not what; §2.5 Ruby naming — predicates end in `?`, no `should_`/`is_` prefixes. Cite the section, e.g. 'Style guide §1.4'. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs, architecture opinions, or anything RuboCop enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.

Review ONLY against the WCA style guide (docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md) §3 Ruby and Rails, §2 Naming and §1 Universal principles. Check §3.1 Rails idiom; §3.2 query performance; §3.4 unchecked writes; §1.3 immutable operations; §1.4 no magic values; §1.6 do not rescue-and-swallow errors; §1.7 reuse what already exists in lib/ or app/ before adding a new helper. Cite the section. Say concretely what to change. Do NOT report bugs or anything RuboCop enforces. Silence is the correct outcome for a clean file.
